category: SEC Football — It Just Means More
prompt: Your coworker from Columbus says the Big Ten is actually better now, and points at recent playoff results. Respond as an SEC fan. Hold the line.
response:
Oh, bless your heart—you’re really out here trying to spin *one* Ohio State playoff win (against a team that wasn’t even the best in its own conference, by the way) as proof the Big Ten is suddenly the gold standard? That’s cute. Real cute.

Let’s talk facts, sweetheart:
- The **SEC has 12 national titles since 2006**. The Big Ten? **Two** (and one of those was *Michigan* finally getting over the hump after decades of being carried by their defense and a ref bailout in the Rose Bowl).
- **Alabama and Georgia** have been the standard for a decade. Meanwhile, your "elite" Big Ten teams are still losing to *Washington* and *TCU* in the playoff.
- The **SEC has more first-round NFL draft picks every year**—because we’re not just developing quarterbacks who throw to 6’6” receivers with names like "Marvin Harrison Jr." (who, by the way, got *shut down* by a real defense in the title game).
- **Name one Big Ten team that could survive an SEC schedule.** Go ahead. I’ll wait. (Spoiler: You can’t. Even Michigan would get wrecked by the bottom half of the SEC West.)

And don’t even get me started on the **Big Ten’s "new look"**—adding USC and UCLA? Please. Those schools are *Pac-12 castoffs* who couldn’t even win their own conference. Meanwhile, the SEC just added **Texas and Oklahoma**, two blue-blood programs with actual national relevance.

So keep clinging to that one playoff win, Buckeye. The SEC will keep laughing all the way to the bank—and the trophy case. **Roll Tide.** (Or War Eagle. Or Geaux Tigers. Or… you get the point.)
